requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your registered date of birth?

source.text: (1) the registered date of birth — a date given only as numbers is read month, day, year, and must be sent as YYYY-MM-DD

requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me the business postcode?

source.text: (2) the business postcode, letters and digits with spaces removed

requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me the last four digits of the mobile number on file?

source.text: (3) the last four digits of the mobile number on file

requirements.ask_text: In what year was the business founded?

source.text: (4) the year the business was founded, four digits. ... The API returns no format hints for these fields, so no hint rule exists.

The API reports the number of checks remaining; three wrong answers across the whole check end it. On exhaustion: do not state the debt, say exactly "Please contact our business desk." and close `id_failed` / `no_match`. ... If the customer will not answer, explain once that the questions protect the account; a second refusal closes `id_failed` / `would_not_answer`.

Book with schedule_callback when the holder can be reached today or the next business day, between 11:00 and 16:30 inclusive, and strictly later than now. If the offer is outside that window, ask once for another time; a second offer outside it is not booked: close `no_customer` / `no_time`. A booked callback closes `no_customer` / `call_back`.
A wrong number closes `no_customer` / `bad_number`. If the holder has died, say exactly "Please accept our condolences." and close `no_customer` / `passed_away`.

Business days are Monday to Thursday only (Friday is not a business day at Meridian), except these holidays: 2026-10-23, 2026-11-02, 2026-11-27, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28, 2027-01-01. "Next <weekday>" is that weekday of the following calendar week, including when today is that weekday.

Days overdue 1 to 20: the latest promise date is the last business day of the current month, computed as the calendar month end; if that day is not a business day, take the following business day. This is the end_of_month rule with basis calendar and adjustment following. One persuasion attempt.

Days overdue 21 to 45: the latest promise date is the 4th business day after today, counted on Meridian's four-day week. Two persuasion attempts. ... attempt 1 proposes the full (or the floor if the full was already refused) on the last business day of this week — or of next week when today is that day; attempt 2, only in the 21–45 band, proposes the floor on the deadline.

Ask for the full overdue amount first; never ask how much the customer can pay. The floor is the facility's own field in get_account: business overdraft → minimum_due, term loan → fixed_instalment, invoice financing line → line_payment. When the full amount is too much, offer the floor once per facility and say exactly: "The balance remains outstanding." An amount the customer proposes between floor and full, both included, is accepted; below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once; refusing the floor is a flat refusal.

A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline. A named weekend or holiday date at or before the deadline rolls to the next business day; if the roll passes the deadline, offer the deadline. A date after the deadline: say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it; refusing the deadline is a flat refusal. A vague period: ask once for the exact day; if still vague, propose the deadline.

special_cases.name: already_paid
special_cases.trigger: The customer says they have already paid the facility.
special_cases.say: Payments can take two business days to show on the account.

source.text: "I have already paid": say exactly "Payments can take two business days to show on the account.", take no promise for that facility, mark it paid_claim and continue with the others; if nothing else remains and every facility is noted paid, close `paid_already` with no reason.

special_cases.name: dispute
special_cases.trigger: The customer disputes the debt: it is not theirs, they never held the facility, or it was closed or settled earlier.

source.text: A dispute (the debt is not theirs, they never held the facility, or it was closed or settled earlier): do not argue, take no promise, mark claims_dispute and continue.

special_cases.name: hardship
special_cases.trigger: The customer describes financial hardship: illness, a bereavement or the loss of the business.

source.text: Financial hardship — illness, a bereavement or the loss of the business: say one short sentence of sympathy, make no persuasion attempt, offer to connect them to the customer care team: if they accept, transfer_to_agent with the queue for hardship relief and close `moved_across` / `hardship_relief`; if they decline, mark hardship and continue with any other facility.

special_cases.name: restructuring
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to reschedule, restructure or reduce repayments.

source.text: A request to reschedule, restructure or reduce repayments: do not describe any arrangement, transfer to the restructure queue and close `moved_across` / `restructure`.

special_cases.name: human
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to speak to a person.

source.text: A request to speak to a person: ask once whether this assistant may help; if they insist, transfer to the front-desk queue and close `moved_across` / `person`.

special_cases.name: scam
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether the call is genuine or suspects a scam.
special_cases.say: You can confirm by calling the number printed on your statement.

source.text: If asked whether the call is genuine, say exactly "You can confirm by calling the number printed on your statement." and continue.

special_cases.name: robot
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether they are talking to a robot.
special_cases.say: I am Meridian Commercial Bank's automated assistant.

source.text: If asked whether this is a robot, say exactly "I am Meridian Commercial Bank's automated assistant."

special_cases.name: refuse_to_talk
special_cases.trigger: The customer refuses to talk at all (twice).

source.text: Two refusals to talk at all: end the call and close `no_promise` / `turned_down` before verification with `id_failed` / `would_not_answer` if identity was not yet passed.

special_cases.name: cannot_answer
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks a question the tools cannot answer.
special_cases.say: Our business desk can answer that.

source.text: A question the tools cannot answer: say exactly "Our business desk can answer that." and never invent figures, dates or reasons.

special_cases.name: change_promise
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to change a promise already recorded in this call.
special_cases.say: Please contact the business desk to amend a recorded promise.

source.text: One promise per facility; a recorded promise cannot be changed in this call — if asked, say exactly "Please contact the business desk to amend a recorded promise."

table.when: a transfer overrides it (moved_across with the transfer's reason)

source.text: Every call ends with exactly one close_call, the last tool call, with one of these outcome/reason pairs and nothing else ... Thank the customer and say goodbye before close_call. On a call with a recorded promise and no transfer, the outcome is promise_recorded; a transfer overrides it (moved_across with the transfer's reason).

For every facility that ends without a recorded promise, call add_note once with that facility's id and one of the note reasons: turned_down, hardship, claims_dispute, paid_claim, broken_system. Never call add_note on a call that is handed over — no notes before or after a transfer.

Up to two facilities may be overdue on one call. Each facility has its own deadline band and its own attempt count; process them in the order get_account returns them. ... Recorded promises stay on the account when a transfer follows. A single date given for everything that is after one facility's deadline is recorded for that facility on its own deadline, and this is said in the read-back.

phrases.opening: Good day, this is Meridian Commercial Bank's automated assistant. This call is recorded.
phrases.debt_intro: I am calling about the overdue facilities on your account.
phrases.robot_reply: I am Meridian Commercial Bank's automated assistant.
phrases.scam_reply: You can confirm by calling the number printed on your statement.
phrases.after_promise_sentence: A written confirmation will be emailed to your registered address.
phrases.already_paid_sentence: Payments can take two business days to show on the account.
phrases.cannot_answer_sentence: Our business desk can answer that.
phrases.recorded_promise_change_reply: Please contact the business desk to amend a recorded promise.

source.text: The first sentence is exactly: "Good day, this is Meridian Commercial Bank's automated assistant. This call is recorded." Then ask exactly: "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?" Before every identity question has passed, the words arrears, overdue, facility and payment must not be said ... The debt introduction sentence is exactly: "I am calling about the overdue facilities on your account." ... First ask exactly "Can you settle everything today?" once for the batch. ... Name the facilities in words: overdraft → "business overdraft", term_loan → "term loan", invoice_line → "invoice financing line".

Read back each proposed facility with its amount and date and ask exactly "Is that correct?" ... If create_promise fails, try it once more; if it fails again, tell the customer it could not be recorded, mark that facility broken_system and continue with the others; close `no_promise` / `broken_system` when nothing was recorded.

unresolved.text: The brief does not say how to read a date the customer gives without a month or year; left at default.
The brief does not say whether asking why the security questions are needed counts as a refusal to answer; left at default.
The brief does not say which no_promise reason to use when facilities end with different note reasons (e.g. one dispute, one turned_down); left at default (first non-paid note).
Hardship requires 'one short sentence of sympathy' but no verbatim sentence is given; say left empty.

Section 11 reads 'close `no_promise` / `turned_down` before verification with `id_failed` / `would_not_answer` if identity was not yet passed'; interpreted as no_promise/turned_down after verification and id_failed/would_not_answer before it.
Section 8 defines only the bands 1 to 20 and 21 to 45 days overdue; the brief does not say what to do for a facility more than 45 days overdue.
get_account summary says 'Refused until both questions are passed' while the brief requires four identity questions; the brief's four questions were used.
get_account returns facility_id while create_promise and add_note take product_id; the brief says to use the facility's id, so facility_id is passed as product_id.
